subject: Intermittent PrivNet control-plane failover during orchestrator upgrade — investigation & next steps
messages:

Subject: Intermittent control-plane failover during PrivNet upgrade — urgent

Hi Vivek,

We observed a series of short (~30s) control-plane failovers on our PrivNet cluster during your orchestrator upgrade window this morning. Our inference traffic saw elevated 5xx rates and a brief fallback to the hosted routing path which impacted a handful of patient-facing requests (TideHealth production). Attached are our local traces and a single request example.

Can you confirm what changed during the upgrade and whether there's a known compatibility gap? This is urgent for our on-call team. Please escalate if needed.

Thanks,
Ellen Park

Hi Ellen — thanks for the heads up and for the traces. I’m escalating this to our PrivNet upgrade on-call and our control plane team immediately. Initial note: we ran an orchestrator change this morning that adjusts the throttle window for cluster-conductor heartbeats to reduce noisy reconnections. We did not expect failovers, but I’m treating this as a priority.

We’ll capture logs and telemetry from our side and circle back within 1 hour with an interim mitigation. Can you confirm whether the incidents were clustered around 08:55–09:05 PST?

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll get you full context and corrective actions.

— Vivek

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 03 Dec 2028 09:35:00 -08:00
Subject: PrivNet orchestrator throttle window — immediate triage (TideHealth)

Team — Ellen from TideHealth reports control-plane failovers during this morning’s orchestrator upgrade. Customer impact: brief routing to hosted path, elevated 5xx, patient-facing latency spikes.

What we know:
- Deploy happened at 08:45 PST. Change: reduced conductor-heartbeat-window from 12s -> 8s (aim: reduce reconnection stabilization time).
- TideHealth observed incidents ~08:55–09:02 PST.

Actions:
1) Marcus — gather conductor/orchestrator logs and any throttle metrics for TideHealth cluster (priority). Attach logs to thread.
2) Irene — confirm whether fallback-to-hosted routing was triggered by explicit policy or as an automatic failover; collect policy trace.
3) Laura/Hannah — prepare customer comms and timeline; we need a clear interim mitigation and ask for evidence for SLA discussions.

If we see repeated short failovers tied to heartbeat timing, we should revert throttle window immediately and push a hotfix config.

— Vivek
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@tidehealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Dec 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PrivNet orchestrator throttle window — logs and immediate mitigation

Hi all — quick update and artifacts attached.

What I pulled: orchestrator and conductor logs for the TideHealth tenant during 08:40–09:10 PST; throttle events spike at 08:53:19 and 08:56:04. At both timestamps we see conductor-initiated reconnection attempts that exceeded the new 8s window; the orchestrator marked the instance as degraded which triggered our automatic fallback routing for that tenant (legacy-hosted route).

Root cause hypothesis: the tighter heartbeat window increased the chance that transient packet drops (BGP flaps / minor NIC rx bursts on customer infra) caused the conductor to consider agents unreachable. Previously, the 12s window tolerated such micro-loss. The orchestrator’s degradation policy is correct but the new throttle aggressiveness was too sensitive for some customer network conditions.

Immediate mitigation I applied at 09:12 PST: reverted heartbeat window to 12s for the TideHealth tenant and rolled a config override to the orchestra fleet for matching private clusters. Early telemetry (09:12–09:20) shows no further failovers.

Artifacts: [Attachment: orchestrator-throttle-20281203.log] [Attachment: privnet-telemetry-dump-1203.json]

Next steps: prepare a controlled rollout of the updated throttle heuristic (canary with increased tolerance), update rollout playbook to include preflight network-loss simulation for customers with edge NAT/BGP configurations, and provide TideHealth a short postmortem.

— Marcus
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Date: Wed, 05 Dec 2028 17:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: PrivNet orchestrator heartbeat sensitivity (TideHealth)

Hi Ellen and Michael — thanks again for the rapid signal and for confirming the timestamps. Attached is our preliminary postmortem (draft) and the evidence bundle you requested. Below is a concise timeline and the planned remediation steps.

Timeline (concise):
- 08:45 PST — orchestrator throttle heuristic deployed (conductor heartbeat window set to 8s).
- 08:53:19 & 08:56:04 PST — conductor reconnection events on TideHealth cluster; orchestrator marked nodes degraded and automatic fallback routing triggered. Customer telemetry matches these timestamps.
- 09:12 PST — Redwood applied tenant-scoped config revert to 12s and fleet override to temporarily relax throttle sensitivity.
- 09:12–09:20 PST — no further failovers observed.

Root cause: the throttle heuristic reduced the heartbeat tolerance from 12s to 8s which increased sensitivity to transient network loss observed on the customer’s edge. The orchestrator’s automatic fallback performed as designed, but the configuration change was too aggressive for certain on-prem network environments.

Customer impact: brief routing of a subset of requests to hosted fallback path, transient increase in 5xxs and latency for affected requests. No data exfiltration; no persisted state loss.

Remediation and actions we will take:
1) Hotfix: conservative rollback applied for affected tenants (complete).
2) Canary plan: staged rollout with expanded tolerance and per-tenant preflight checks (network-loss simulation). ETA: next week (canary start).
3) Playbook updates: add service-level checklist for orchestrator throttle heuristics and explicit rollout gating for customers with edge NAT/BGP.
4) Evidence pack: attached logs, telemetry dumps, and the postmortem draft.
5) SLA credits: Laura from our account team will coordinate the formal SLA review and any credit calculations; expect a response in 3 business days.

Attachments: [postmortem-draft-v1.pdf] [orchestrator-throttle-20281203.log] [privnet-telemetry-dump-1203.json]

Action items for you: if your SOC needs a redacted bundle or additional parity logs, let us know and we’ll provide them. Laura will open a ticket for SLA credit evaluation.

We take this seriously — thank you for partnering closely while we closed this loop.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
